confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from aggregated cost-of-living data I found by web search in November 2026. Numbeo's Seattle page gives an inexpensive meal at about $25 (range $18-40), a mid-range three-course meal for two at about $100, a cappuccino at about $6.63-6.89 and a 0.5 L domestic draft beer at about $8. Wise gives a meal at about $21, a cappuccino at about $6.11 and beer at about $8. Expatistan gives a cappuccino at about $7, and livingcost.net gives a pint at $9.45. Cocktail and wine prices come from Seattle-specific blog and guide ranges, not price indexes, so they are less certain: cocktails were about $13-18 downtown and wine about $8-14 for a standard glass, rising to $16 or more at premium or waterfront venues. Happy-hour prices are much lower and were left out. These are crowdsourced or modelled figures for late 2026 used as a stand-in for July 2026. Accommodation anchors are my own estimates from general knowledge only, with no searches or listings checked. They assume July is peak season, with summer tourism and the cruise season raising rates. Actual nightly rates could easily be 20-30% higher or lower depending on events, neighbourhood and booking timing.
comparable_city_reasoning: Seattle is a high-cost US West Coast city. I checked the food and drink anchors against similar cities like San Francisco, Boston and San Diego, which a 2025 Expatistan-based comparison found tied with Seattle at $18 for a downtown cocktail. Accommodation is based on general knowledge of peak-summer pricing in high-cost US cities with few hostel options (a small number of downtown hostels and limited budget hotel supply near the centre).
